sections.title: Situation
sections.prompt: What is the real problem, by when, and which numbers frame it?
criteria: Separates two problems: a go-live that depends on one person, and a person who needs clear feedback and support
Derives the harness finishing around week 14 at Dana's recent rate (15 days at about 1.1 a week)
Derives the team's 10 engineer-days of slack and the 9-day shortfall if nothing changes
States what isn't known yet (the cause) and doesn't guess at it

sections.title: Stakeholders
sections.prompt: Who has a stake, what does each want, and how do you bring them along?
criteria: Puts Dana first, with what Dana needs: clear expectations, privacy and support
Includes the HR partner, your manager, the chain and the peers doing extra reviews
Says what Lee takes on and what comes off Lee's plate
Ends with one idea that ties the stakeholders together

sections.title: Options
sections.prompt: What are the real options, and how does each do on the go-live and on fairness?
criteria: Includes waiting and covering quietly as an option
Shows that a formal PIP now is blocked because no feedback is documented
Shows that removing Dana now is unfair and loses the harness knowledge
Compares options on one table with the same criteria

sections.title: Decision and Trade-offs
sections.prompt: What do you do, what do you give up, and what would make you change course?
criteria: Makes one clear call that both moves the critical path and starts a fair feedback process
Names what is given up, including Dana's ownership of the harness and Lee's own work
Says the re-plan is reversible and a formal process is not to be started lightly
Gives a dated checkpoint (week 4) with written criteria

sections.title: Economics
sections.prompt: What does each option cost, in credits, revenue at risk, contractor spend and backfill?
criteria: Prices waiting as about 8 weeks of credits ($320k) and the $4.8M termination right
Prices the contractor from hours and rate ($36k) and the engineer-days it adds
Prices an exit as a backfill cost and a 4-month vacancy that lands after go-live
Labels the assumed figures (rate, focus, backfill)

sections.title: Org and Ownership
sections.prompt: Who owns what on the team for the next 10 weeks?
criteria: Gives the harness one owner who isn't Dana, with Dana on a defined part
Gives the contractor bounded, non-critical work
Keeps you as owner of the feedback process, with HR as partner

sections.title: Plan and Milestones
sections.prompt: What happens week by week, for the project and for Dana?
criteria: Has the direct conversation in week 0, before any re-plan is announced
Lands the harness by week 6 under the new owner
Has written check-ins for Dana at weeks 2 and 4
Has a measurable project gate before go-live

sections.title: Risk and Governance
sections.prompt: What keeps this fair, documented and lawful?
criteria: Writes expectations as observable facts with dates, not judgments about character
Offers support (EAP, leave, flexibility) and doesn't ask for medical details
Brings HR in before the conversation and before any formal step
Protects against retaliation if Dana takes leave

sections.title: Metrics
sections.prompt: How do you know it's working, for the project and for Dana?
criteria: Pairs each success metric with a guard metric
Tracks harness completion and accuracy against the 97% gate
Tracks peer review workload and after-hours work as a guard on the team
Tracks that promised support was actually given, as a fairness guard

sections.title: Communication
sections.prompt: What does each audience hear, and what stays private?
criteria: Gives a one-line message for at least four audiences
Keeps Dana's situation private from the team and the customer
Tells your manager the risk and the plan in numbers
Sets a cadence for check-ins
